items.title: Scientists discover a hidden “ID card” in cat urine
items.summary: Cats may identify one another through a surprisingly durable chemical “calling card” made from 13 unusual fatty acids in their urine. The compounds appear linked to mysterious fat droplets in the kidneys and may represent a scent-recognition system shared across the cat family.

items.title: Scientists may have solved a 2,000-year-old Dead Sea Scrolls mystery
items.summary: Researchers may have solved a long-running mystery surrounding the Dead Sea Scrolls by proposing that the Qumran sect really did use its distinctive 364-day calendar. items.title: New nanoparticles make hidden chemical differences light up
items.summary: Scientists have developed ultra-bright nanoparticles that can detect tiny amounts of chemicals and distinguish between molecules that look almost identical. The technology could one day provide a cheaper way to catch dangerous drug impurities or trace pollutants using simple low-cost lasers.

items.title: Ancient DNA reveals how plague kept returning for 400 years after the Black Death
items.summary: Ancient DNA reveals that plague repeatedly returned to Europe for more than 400 years after the Black Death, evolving into new lineages and spreading through trade, migration, and war. items.title: A 66-million-year-old tooth reveals T. rex was nearly as warm as a human
items.summary: Chemical clues preserved inside fossilized T. rex teeth reveal that the dinosaur maintained a body temperature of about 97 degrees Fahrenheit, almost identical to humans. items.summary: Physicists have detected strong evidence that heavy, fleeting Z bosons can become quantum entangled during Higgs boson decays at CERN’s Large Hadron Collider. items.title: Hurricane Hunters reveal 4 warning signs that a storm is about to strengthen
items.summary: Nearly three decades of Hurricane Hunter data reveal four features that can help a tilted tropical cyclone straighten its circulation and become capable of intensifying. The findings could give forecasters an earlier warning that a seemingly disorganized storm is becoming primed to strengthen.

items.title: A deadly ebola relative is surging after years in the shadows
items.summary: A growing Bundibugyo virus outbreak is showing how a little-known relative of Ebola can become a major threat when diagnosis and treatment options are limited. Experts warn that preparing only for familiar pathogens could leave the world vulnerable when rare but deadly viruses suddenly reemerge.

items.title: At an old steel site in Pittsburgh, bacteria evolved to survive—and eat—industrial pollution
items.summary: Across Appalachia and the Rust Belt region, including throughout the city of Pittsburgh, former industrial sites are being transformed into new neighborhoods, research centers and technology hubs.

items.title: Reconstructing the Great Miami Hurricane of 1926
items.summary: The first storm warning for the Miami area wasn't issued until only a few hours before the powerful cyclone made landfall just south of downtown, leaving residents with little time to prepare for what would become the hurricane of their nightmares.

items.title: Australia's vast Nullarbor Plain hides deep caves that can teach us about alien worlds
items.summary: Stretching more than 200,000 square kilometers (77,000 square miles) across southern Australia, the vast, flat plains of the Nullarbor mark one of the world's largest regions of limestone. It formed when an ancient shallow sea retreated some 14 million years ago.

items.title: Bringing ice sheets to life: Releasing a dynamic ice sheet modeling workflow for Australia's climate model
items.summary: Ice sheets are fundamental components of the Earth system. Antarctica and Greenland, the two ice sheets currently on Earth, don't just affect their own regions: What happens on these vast masses of land ice influences weather, climate, society and the environment around the planet.

items.summary: Researchers at the Department of Energy's (DOE) Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL) have released LandScan Mosaic, a next-generation global population distribution dataset that estimates where people are by modeling how buildings are used and occupied throughout the day. items.title: How narwhal 'scientists' track Arctic warming
items.summary: The fight against climate change has a new, spiral-tusked ally: the narwhal.

items.title: Meet Earth's newest wild cat species, the first named in over a century
items.summary: A previously unknown cat species has been identified in plain sight: at a wildlife sanctuary in Bolivia, where the small, spotted feline had been living for years.

items.title: A humpback whale was spotted in a California river, 60 miles from its Pacific Ocean home
items.summary: Denny Glover was hoping for a big catch when he went fishing with buddies on the Sacramento River, but he wasn't expecting a fully grown humpback whale.

items.title: Rethinking how we assess students could improve their well-being
items.summary: When you were in school, what stressed you out the most? For many students, classroom assessments—graded tests, quizzes, group work, presentations, labs and the like—would be near the top of the list.
